title: Rail8 flow file, schemaVersion 1 (draft — review at hand-over, P0-12)
description: One flow: where messages come from, how they are delivered and recorded, the finite limits every flow has, and the ordered steps. Component- and step-specific keys are passed through to the component's or step's own configSchema at deploy time.

id.description: Flow id, unique in its package; the identity is tenant / package / flow:id @ version.

from.description: The consumer endpoint this flow listens on, plus the component's own options.

mode.description: ARCHITECTURE §4 message lifecycle per delivery mode.

saveTimeout.description: at-least-once: the durable save deadline before NACK/503 (default 5s).

timeout.description: Every mode: the time each run of a message has; its deadline is the run's start plus this (sync after admission, each at-least-once claim). When it passes the run stops: the step it is in is interrupted, no later step or send starts, a send already started is cut by its producer, and the history says why. Positive and at most 24h; default 30s.

queue.description: at-least-once only: the work queue behind the durable save; absent or postgres = the node's Postgres work queue; kafka names the optional Kafka add-on (O-1), not in this build: refused at deploy (D-075).

retries.description: at-least-once only (refused at load on sync and at-most-once): the schedule of a failed message's retries (CORE-14a, D-135 draft). A failed run waits interval × multiplier^(k−1), capped at maxInterval, before retry k — a work item with a not-before time, never a sleeping thread — and after count + 1 runs the message is parked at step 1. Omitted = the node's RAIL8_RETRIES_COUNT / RAIL8_RETRIES_INTERVAL (3 × 5m). The durations are checked at load: interval 1s..24h, maxInterval interval..24h.

count.description: Retries after the first run; 0 = park at the first failure.

interval.description: The wait before the first retry, 1s..24h.

multiplier.description: Growth of the wait per retry; default 1.

maxInterval.description: Cap of the wait, from the interval to 24h; default the interval.

limits.description: Every flow has a finite max body size; never a default of unlimited (CLAUDE.md).

maxInFlight.description: Admission budget: requests in flight for this flow. Omitted = the runtime's finite default (cores × 2 for CPU-heavy flows, ARCHITECTURE §4), never unlimited.

maxInFlightBytes.description: Admission budget: bytes in flight for this flow. Omitted = the runtime's finite default (per-flow byte budget, ARCHITECTURE §14), never unlimited.

partitionBy.description: at-least-once: the key of the flow's one extractKey step (no split or to before it; earlier steps do not apply to the key), evaluated at the durable save on the received body; items of one key run one at a time in accept order; no value = unordered, over 256 characters = refused (400). No effect on sync and at-most-once flows (D-075).

forwardHeaders.description: Allow-list of ingress headers that reach producers; nothing propagates implicitly.

retry.description: Per-step retry policy for steps marked retryable: exponential backoff between initial and max.

processes.description: Local processes: named blocks of steps, each run inside the same message where a step of type process calls it, its steps numbered in run order and named <call>/<step>. A process may call another; one that calls itself, directly or through others, is refused when the flow loads. A process no step calls is allowed.

keyName.description: a key or prop name; one that starts with 'rail8.' is the platform's own and refused

type.description: Step type. The schema knows the typed requirements of xslt, xsd, route, to, extractKey, validate, split and process; any other type passes here and is checked against its step's own configSchema at deploy time (an unknown type, e.g. a typo, fails there, not here).

name.description: Step name (camelCase allowed): the step's label in a message's history and per-step timings, and what a search by step finds. Optional: a step without one is named after its type, a process call after the process it calls. Names, given or not, are unique in the flow's steps and in each process's (checked when the flow loads); ingress is the arrival's name and no step's.

stylesheet.description: Path of the XSLT file from the package root (D-078); an include or import inside it is relative to the including file. Stays inside the package.

schema.description: Path of the XSD file from the package root (D-078); an include or import inside it is relative to the including file. Stays inside the package.

xpath.description: Selects the parts; every selected node becomes a child message.

process.description: The process of this flow file whose steps run here; the call takes no other key.
